evidence_items.publisher: Cognition; Jerry Fodor and Zenon Pylyshyn
evidence_items.explanation: The original paper establishes the historical concern about compositional and systematic representations. Its March publication is recorded conservatively at month end; it does not establish the performance of modern models.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Najoung Kim, Tal Linzen and Paul Smolensky
evidence_items.explanation: Controlled changes to COGS exposed failures to transfer familiar linguistic components into new contexts in T5. This directly supports persistence of compositional generalization problems, rather than merely unfamiliar-word recognition problems.

The evaluation finds persistent errors across a broad collection of reasoning and knowledge tasks and multiple model families. The same section reports improvement with model scale and examples, so these results support remaining weaknesses rather than no progress.

The study shows that prompting can improve the composition of intermediate answers. This limits a stronger interpretation that the old problems had seen no meaningful progress, but does not establish their general solution.

unresolved_gaps: These evaluations do not test every historical criticism or every neural architecture.
